newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips after trade, spec selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips after trade, spec selling.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures lost ground in the afternoon session on Monday after early buying faded and trade and speculative sales speeded up, traders said.
Turnover totalled 11,175 lots including a fairly large spread volume, particularly in March 97/March 98 at 60 stg a tonne. Dec/March spread was under pressure.
"London had a rally this morning but some one sold the stuff out. There is no real fresh news. The market is just stuck in a range," said one trader.
The third-month March contract dominated activity and ended three stg off at 1,012 stg. It had risen to a session high of 1,025 stg in early deals.
December lost five stg to close at 987 stg a tonne.
Traders described the CFTC Commitment of Traders Report released on Friday as friendly with net speculative long positions plunging to 4,500 lots.
But industry appetite continued to be marginal at current price levels.

The market's focus is likely to shift in the coming weeks to third quarter grind figures which traders generally expected to rise steadily, and on first arrivals from Ivory Coast where the new 1996/97 cocoa season is due to start in mid-October.
Traders said a slow start in Ivorian arrivals could push up the December switch while one leading trader holds a hefty amount of cocoa delivered against September.
